newsitem.title: UK: UK public spending to limit scope for tax cuts - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK public spending to limit scope for tax cuts - FT.

text.p: UK government ministers are this week expected to set next year's public spending total at a level that will rule out significant tax cuts in the November 26 budget, the Financial Times newspaper reported.

Despite efforts by the Treasury to secure savings, the spending total for 1997 to 1998 -- called the control total -- is expected to be fixed at only a little less than the 268.2 billion stg pencilled in a year ago, the newspaper said.

A special cabinet meeting on Tuesday will hear a presentation of spending plans for next year proposed by a ministerial committee in charge of expenditure negotiations and chaired by UK finance minister Kenneth Clarke.
"The reduction in the control total could emerge at two billion stg but certainly no more than three billion stg," the Financial Times quoted a minister as saying.
Given the commitment from Clarke to reduce public borrowing as a first priority, this would allow net tax cuts totalling perhaps only two billion stg, the newspaper said.

Ministers are expecting the basic rate of income tax to be reduced by about one pence to 23 pence, coupled with an increase to more than 4,000 stg in the income band at which the 20 pence starting rate of tax is payable, the Financial Times said.
